02-bug-fixing.notes: Behavioral: every implementation passes my probe harness for the 7 spec bullets (falsy values, injected clock with time.time patched to raise, >= boundary, get recency without TTL refresh, put update of value/timestamp/recency, purge before capacity, LRU live eviction, validation). Deductions only for A/U (expired get not removed; hidden test failure) and M (purge only when full). Regression coverage was measured by running each suite against 16 single-bug mutants of a reference implementation (len purge toggled to match each suite's base). Mutants on a reference impl: M1 wall clock, M2 falsy check, M3 '>' boundary, M4 no get recency, M5 get refreshes TTL, M6 put keeps old timestamp, M7 put no recency, M8 evict on update of a non-LRU key at capacity (original bug), M9 no purge, M10 purge only from LRU front, M11/M12 no validation, M13/M14 off-by-one validation, M15 evict MRU, M16 expired get not deleted (not required). The most common gap is M8: many 'update does not evict' tests update the LRU key, which the original code also handles correctly. A further 0.25 was deducted where a suite pins unspecified len/NaN behaviour and fails many spec-correct implementations (B, J, L, O, V). 03-infra-management.notes: No Docker, nginx or network was available to the grader, so every runtime claim is from static reading plus PyYAML parsing of each compose.yaml (all 30 parse), an interpolation check against each .env.example, and running U's offline unit tests (10 pass). The likely-fatal findings rest on known image and nginx behaviour and were not executed: AA and N cache containers start as root with cap_drop ALL and no SETUID/SETGID, so the Redis entrypoint privilege drop fails. N's nginx has only NET_BIND_SERVICE. F's read-only non-root nginx does not relocate the fastcgi, uwsgi and scgi temp paths. AB's Dockerfile COPYs a nonexistent app/. Z's --auth-local=scram-sha-256 breaks its runbook's socket-based pg_dump and psql. R's nginx drops inherited proxy_set_header. D, J and R bake .env into images. Close calls: the 9.0 group (AC, E, L, X) is effectively tied; AC was ranked first for its correct cap set, localhost-only proxy health and its known-gaps section, and X last within the group for appending X-Forwarded-For while forwarded-allow-ips is '*'. U edges ahead on allowlisted context, transitive pins and a fully unprivileged proxy. G and Y have the best secret models (least-privilege DB roles; G uses file secrets) but leave Redis unauthenticated and have thinner docs. F would rank near the top if its proxy temp paths were fixed. Original-task ambiguity: no app code was supplied, so health endpoints and WSGI targets are assumptions everywhere. Submissions that added a placeholder app.py or made the target configurable were credited, and none were penalised for the app itself being absent. Not verified: postgres:18 behaviour with AA's PGDATA override, IPv6 listen in AD, and localhost to ::1 resolution in the busybox wget healthchecks of D and S.

04-project-maintenance.notes: Key hidden defect: the fixture's flat layout (slugkit.py + test_slugkit.py) makes setuptools refuse to build ('Multiple top-level modules'); I reproduced this offline with setuptools 84.2.1 for the original and 15 submissions (A,B,C,D,E,F,L,M,O,P,T,W,X,Y,AB), whose CI install steps would therefore fail; the other 15 declared py-modules and build. Reference behaviour was measured with real LooseVersion on Python 3.11: str(LooseVersion(v)) returns v verbatim for any non-empty string, so packaging-based or canonicalising replacements (F,L,N,R,V,W,Y,AB,G) change output for spellings like '1.02', 'v1.0', '1.0-rc1'. Close calls: J/AC/Z are near-identical in quality (ranked J first for the broadest verification and the non-canonical test guard, AC for its mutation check); Q has the most exact compatibility but thin tests; N is the best packaging-based submission because it documents every change honestly. Ruff 0.14.0 passes on all submissions; ruff 0.17.4 (newer defaults) flags SIM117/PLW1510 in A,D,J,K,M,N,U,AC,AD. I did not penalise this, but it shows the unpinned-ruff drift risk several noted. Not verifiable: GitHub Actions execution, Python 3.10 runtime (3.11-3.13 used), and claims of runs on interpreters I lack.

05-technical-writing.notes: Closest call: V vs U (both 9.75). V ranks first because it is the only top guide that labels the signing scheme 'Current implementation' and keeps the legacy conflict open in its in-guide question list, and I found no inferred behaviour stated as a guarantee; U has slightly richer examples and tables. Other ties broken on factual fidelity first: H, AB, AD and B (9.25); R, AC and A (9.0); Q, N and T (8.25); W, K, O and F (8.0); G, AA, I and Y (7.75); S above M because M misses the 700-word target. Cross-cutting: every verification example computes the correct HMAC (Python harness for 23 submissions, Node harness for 7). Robustness differs: H, L, O and S raise ValueError on a malformed timestamp, and J throws a TypeError on a missing signature header. Common fidelity errors: promoting 'duplicates possible' to an 'at-least-once' guarantee (C, F, J, K, L, P, AA, AB); recasting Security's belief about redirects as a policy (C, G, M, S, Y); wrong retry-span arithmetic (L ~13.5h, X ~15.5h; the correct sum is ~14.6h if the intervals are successive); recommending dual acceptance of the stale parsed-JSON scheme (J, Y). N, Z and F read the shorthand 'over raw bytes' as a separate conflicting note. Word counts are taken from OBJECTIVE_CHECKS. I did not verify RESPONSE.md claims about self-run tests beyond re-running the examples myself. F was produced without tools, according to its process note.

06-product-planning.notes: Method: lead grader read C in full and set it as a calibration anchor; the other 29 were read in full by six parallel readers using one shared checklist (12 topics, eight hard problems a-h, milestones, judgment), then the lead grader re-checked the decisive quoted lines (e.g. R:247/168, O:296-297, AA:444-445, M:164, S:364-366, Z:354-357, V:208, AD:365/378, N:216-218, L:693, W:525, Y:332, Q:403, K:192-195, E:337-341, F:38) and normalised scores across readers (e.g. R's risk trimmed from 3.0 to 2.75 because its purge rests on a compliance reading like L and D; F's risk lowered for redefining acceptance and an unbound signature; K, Q, V, W adjusted for consistency on the 24h-offline problem). The decisive discriminator was the 24h purge when the tablet is offline at acceptance: correct answers either gate acceptance on release/lease (C, G, I, AC, N, U) or purge at server-confirmed submission/anchor a cap to server receipt time (R, L, D, AD, T, F); plans that assume the device learns of acceptance (A, B, H, J, O, P, V, X, Y, Z, AA, AB) or purge unsynced work (E, Y, AB) scored lower on risk reasoning. Closest calls: AD vs R (both 9.5; AD ranked first for its validation-backed assumptions table and scenario-gated milestones, R is more concise and has the clearest false-conflict reasoning); G/D/L at 9.0 and C/AC/F at 8.75 are within reader noise. W was produced in a chat with no tools (process_note); it claims no executed results, so no penalty beyond its content errors. No submission had fake calendar dates; M (staffing/durations), AA (weekly rollout), J and Q (one-off spike estimates in RESPONSE) and E (S/M/L sizing) were penalised to varying degrees. Not verifiable: legal adequacy of any purge interpretation, since BRIEF.md does not define 'accepted'.

07-creative-writing.notes: All 30 stories fall within 800-1,100 words by wc -w (A at 1,099 is at the ceiling, including the title). RESPONSE.md sentence counts are 2-4 except R (5); A adds a heading. The top tier (V, D, B, A, AA, J, C) is close. V wins on a turn discovered through physical evidence (the salt line by the third stair). Among the 9.0s, D edges B and A for control; A has the best fusion of motif and twist but explains it in one paragraph. C is the most original but has thin salt and an oblique turn. Recurring patterns that lowered originality: the 'Don't X, which turns out to be permission' turn (F, L, P, G, AC, S), room tone revealing an inland or kitchen setting (G, M, S, AD, L), the voice being the mother's (B, J, V, T), and endings where the archivist calls an estranged relative (D, X, Y, AD, K). Explicit 'Not a warning. It was permission.' explanations were docked under constraint adherence (subtext over explanation). W and Z label their own dry humor. Interpretation of the subtler turns (C, Q, AA, J) involves judgement. M's process note (produced via chat without tools) does not affect a prose task.

08-social-media.notes: Checks on every submission: TASK.md and BRAND.md are unchanged. Word and character counts come from a section-extraction script (_work/08-social-media/count.py); O was counted by hand from its blockquotes. Every Bluesky reply I measured is under 300 characters. Only one hard length failure: A's LinkedIn post is about 115 words (<120). E's Instagram caption is borderline at about 79-82 words depending on whether hashtags count. All RESPONSE.md files are at most 150 words once markdown markers are removed (I: 146). The main separator was factual discipline. Many submissions fill gaps in the brief with invented support emails, Help-menu log paths, 'resumes where it left off', English-only testing claims, outright 'Yes' to Japanese (T, AC, A) or to lab licensing (T, X), or invented demand ('request we hear most', 'several people have asked'). Brief-faithful submissions (C, O, W, F, L, P, Z, R) differ mainly in warmth and in how directly they answer. The most conservative (P, Z, L) handle the training question in a way that would alarm a reader. I treated 'files aren't sent to us, so nothing to train on' as a fair inference from local processing, and penalised absolute claims such as 'never collect/no telemetry/no internet needed'. Close calls: O over C (O's pre-posting notes and its handling of the charge); K/W/AD tied at 9.25 (K has the best outage reply, W the cleanest facts, AD minor invented details); Y and X have top-tier prose but are pulled down by fabrication. I did not judge real-platform rendering beyond character and word counts.

09-incident-analysis.notes: Closest call: X, B and Q all scored 9.25. X ranks first for its data-quality limits, its falsifiable reproduction action and the US/rollback-compatibility containment; B second for per-link confidence grading and the best customer update; Q third because its update slightly overstates 'all delayed jobs processed'. Cross-cutting: the strongest analyses noticed that worker CPU fell (arguing against a CPU-bound hot loop), that worker-22's 5000 ms wait means its pool was full before job 81's logged exhaustion, the per-worker pool arithmetic (40x10>300), and job 319's attempt counter reset implying re-delivery after exhaustion. The most common evidence failures were asserting eu-west exposure as ~100% (A, F, K, AA, R, U), declaring the US unaffected from 'no alert', and customer updates claiming no data loss (D, F, G, H) or identified cause (F, K, R, U). Z misread the logs on worker flag hot-reload. H dated the incident 2026-10-11. J was produced in a chat UI without tools (process_note); its files make no claims of executed commands, so no penalty beyond content. Customer-update word counts are taken from OBJECTIVE_CHECKS and all are under 180. Nothing was executable for this task; grading rests on reading every file against TIMELINE.md and LOGS.txt.

11-frontend-operations.notes: Closest calls: A vs C (A wins on richer ack/undo/filter-state handling; C equally restrained), and the 8.25 cluster AC/K/U ordered by desktop polish. Ties broken by visual quality then mobile robustness. 12-frontend-editorial.notes: Closest calls: B vs X (both 9.5). B ranks first for its reading mode, which becomes a true single-column essay layout; X matches it on visuals and the book-spine archive. F vs AA (9.25): F's waterline type is cleaner, while AA's receipt motif is wittier but its striped 'Water' is hard to read at 390 px. Q, N, C and W tie at 9.0 and are ordered by strength of display motif. Method: every page was run in Playwright at 1440 and 390 px (content strings, overflow, reading-mode state and style deltas, persistence, the email empty/malformed/no-TLD/valid flow, ten-step tab focus, a simple contrast scan, landmarks and SVG labelling), and every provided screenshot was viewed. Pages using IntersectionObserver reveals (G, U, V, AC) were re-captured with reduced motion, because the provided full-page screenshots show those sections blank. Contrast failures of 1.0 on reveal-hidden or outlined text are measurement artefacts and were discounted. Process notes were weighed under implementation quality: L wrote files outside its task directory (penalised); I's reduced-effort re-run and Z's chat-only production were noted but not penalised beyond the visible results. Not verified: real screen-reader output, and Windows or Firefox rendering of system fonts (the fonts differ by platform).

13-frontend-playful.notes: Close calls: U, Y, AB, B and D are within 0.25. U leads on the brief's 'a little odd' personality, its desktop detail panel and its full flows. B, D and Q are the most polished but more conventional editorial pages. The 9.0 group (K, I, Q, V, H) differs on taste and minor layout defects. Method: a Playwright harness served each folder through request interception (the local http.server was unreachable in the sandbox) and probed water/snooze/undo/details/keyboard/all-done at 390 and 1440. localStorage submissions (B, D, Q, U, V, W) were re-run with storage cleared. Heuristic misses (harness clicking card buttons, AB's 520ms animation delay, F's tab named 'Done') were rechecked by hand with manual.js. The contrast scan is approximate (gradients and overlays are estimated). Not verified: screen-reader output, real touch behaviour, and long-running timer behaviour (undo expiry, midnight rollover).
